page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i4r.4xlarge is an x86_64 virtualization instance deployed via KVM, designed for workloads requiring a high memory-to-vCPU ratio paired with local storage. It is powered by a dedicated 16-vCPU Intel Xeon 8369B processor operating at a clock speed of 2.7 GHz. The system provides 128.0 GB of system memory, maintaining an allocation ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU, with baseline network bandwidth provisioned at 10 Gbps.

A defining hardware feature of the ecs.i4r.4xlarge instance is its integrated local storage configuration, comprising 959 GB of direct-attached solid-state drive (SSD) storage. The server does not include GPU acceleration hardware, focusing its physical footprint entirely on general compute, high RAM density, and fast local disk access. Network connectivity provides a 10 Gbps baseline, and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default.

From an architectural standpoint, the combination of 128 GB of RAM and 959 GB of local SSD storage makes this instance cost-efficient for applications that demand high throughput without relying exclusively on networked block storage. The tradeoff inherent to local SSD volumes is the requirement for application-level data redundancy, as local storage lacks persistence across certain hardware failure or recreation events. The resource distribution makes it well suited for distributed NoSQL databases, in-memory caching systems, transactional databases, and search indexing nodes.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i4r.4xlarge is an x86_64 instance built on the KVM hypervisor within the Local SSDs instance family. It is equipped with 16 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 8369B processor operating at 2.7 GHz, 128.0 GB of memory offering an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio, and a baseline network throughput of 10 Gbps. It includes 959 GB of integrated local SSD storage, eliminating the latency overhead associated with network-attached block volumes. The instance contains zero GPUs and does not come with complimentary public IPv4 addresses. With its memory-dense profile and low-latency onboard disk capacity, this configuration provides a balanced architecture for memory-heavy and disk-intensive deployments, such as in-memory data grids, distributed search indices, analytics caching layers, and high-performance transactional databases requiring fast local I/O.
